- For the temporary surcharge carveout, legal will want an objective trigger (e.g., GPU spot > X% of baseline for >30 consecutive days) and a maximum surcharge % — we'll propose language.
- Per-invoice bundle credit: that changes cash-flow for us but could be workable if we limit how credits interact with true-ups — will run numbers.

I've looped in Irene (contracts) to draft proposed redline language for the concentration points above. Karthik will patch pricing sensitivity if we move floor amounts.

Claire / team —

Attached is Redwood's marked draft (see comments in Exhibit B). High-level changes we pushed:

1) "Effective Minimum" — replaced the three-floor rows with a defined two-line table: Year 1 minimum (USD) and Year 2 minimum (USD). Language includes: "Effective Minimum means the minimum committed spend for the applicable Year as set forth in the Order Form; any usage below the Effective Minimum shall be invoiced and payable by Customer." This preserves billing clarity.

2) Temporary surcharge carveout — proposed objective trigger text: "If Redwood's average hardware spot cost for the prior 30-day period exceeds the baseline by more than 35%, Redwood may apply a temporary surcharge not to exceed 9% of monthly invoice amount, and in no event for a period longer than 90 days without mutual written agreement." We can negotiate % and duration.

3) Bundle credit application — suggested compromise: apply bundle credits on each invoice, but exclude credits from monthly true-up calculations; annual reconciliation will only consider gross usage and the Effective Minimum. This avoids double-counting credits and limits revenue leakage.

I've put comment pins where we want BrightEdge feedback and where sales ops needs numbers.

Attachments: RDW_Marked_PricingExhibit_v1.docx

Happy to review on the call.

Irene

Irene / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few points from BrightEdge legal: 

- The "Effective Minimum" definition is acceptable but we need an explicit example to avoid month-end proration ambiguity. Please add a short illustrative example showing a partial-month ramp.
- The temporary surcharge trigger is close but the 35% threshold is high for our CFO; request reducing to 25% and limit application to customer cohorts where usage spikes are outside of normal baselines. Also ask for a 60-day maximum.
- On bundle credits: acceptable to apply per-invoice if there is a clear exclusion from true-ups; we'll propose a short clause explaining interaction with credits (we'll send one-line redline tomorrow).

I'll attach our annotated example in the morning. Appreciate keeping the call short and focused — our procurement director (Ethan) will join.
